summary: Adds email search to the user index, plus update and destroy actions and routes. It also adds a welcome email callback on the User model.

findings.title: Search term interpolated into SQL
findings.problem: The index action puts params[:q] straight into the WHERE clause text. Any authenticated caller controls that SQL fragment.
findings.consequence: Any API token holder can read or change arbitrary database rows, including other users' api_token values.
findings.fix: Pass the search term as a bound parameter. Escape LIKE wildcards with sanitize_sql_like.

findings.title: Any user can delete any user
findings.problem: The change exempts destroy from require_admin on line 2. The destroy action then deletes any User by id with no ownership check.
findings.consequence: Any authenticated non-admin can delete every account, including admin accounts.
findings.fix: Remove destroy from the require_admin exemption list. Alternatively, scope the lookup to the current user.

findings.title: Welcome email sent on every save
findings.problem: The model registers send_welcome_email as an after_save callback. That callback fires on updates as well as on creation.
findings.consequence: Users get a new welcome email each time an admin updates their record through the new update action.
findings.fix: Use after_create_commit so the email goes out once, after the insert commits.

findings.title: New behaviour has no covering test
findings.problem: The change adds search, update, destroy and an email callback. The repository has no test or spec directory at all.
findings.consequence: Nothing catches regressions in authorization or callback behaviour on these endpoints.
findings.fix: Add request tests for search, update and destroy with admin and non-admin tokens. Add a model test for the welcome email callback.

dropped.reason: The require_admin filter still guards update, so only admins reach this lookup. Admins may legitimately edit any user.
